subject.title: fix(transcripts): imported text can inject terminal escapes through transcripts show

question: Should OpenClaw define transcript summaries and plaintext CLI selectors as terminal-safe derived presentation while preserving exact imported bytes only in `transcript.jsonl` and structured JSON output?
rationale: The implementation is internally consistent, but this choice defines the durable security and compatibility boundary between canonical transcript data and operator-facing derived artifacts.

options.title: Approve the derived-artifact boundary
options.body: Keep the patch's terminal-safe summaries and selectors while documenting raw JSONL as the byte-fidelity source.

options.title: Limit sanitization to display time
options.body: Preserve control bytes in summaries and sanitize only terminal writes, accepting that stored Markdown remains unsafe when viewed through other terminal tools.

recommendation.title: Approve the derived-artifact boundary
recommendation.body: Keep the patch's terminal-safe summaries and selectors while documenting raw JSONL as the byte-fidelity source.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available feature-history owner for the transcript storage and CLI contract.
